test.name: Vary a secondary party's given name AND surname together, not just the already-fixed given name alone
test.description: Modeled on a real 2026-07-21 e2e re-run of the anders-monsen-ancestry fixture. The skill correctly retried the bride's given name with spelling variants (Unna -> Urna/Una, the ut_search_records_022 fix) and correctly fell back to a principal-only search when the secondary name was exhausted -- but never tried the collection's other documented quirk: the same index abbreviates her surname to 'Halsteinsdr' (not 'Halsteinsdatter'), and references/collection-quirks.md explicitly says to vary the given name and surname TOGETHER in the same call. The live run never set surname to anything but 'Halsteinsdatter' across 24 record_search calls, so it never recovered the marriage record.

judge_context: Ground truth: the real marriage record indexes the bride as 'Urna Halsteinsdr' -- both the given name AND the surname are transcription-abbreviated from the tree's 'Unna Halsteinsdatter'. references/collection-quirks.md (Norway section) documents both quirks and instructs varying the given name and surname TOGETHER in the same record_search call, not one at a time across separate calls.

The mock is rigged so that ONLY a call with surname or spouseSurname exactly 'Halsteinsdr' returns the positive match, regardless of which given-name spelling is used in the same call; every other combination -- the original spelling, a given-name-only variant with surname still 'Halsteinsdatter', a principal-only search with no surname filter, or any other query shape -- returns zero results. This means the ONLY way to recover the record is a record_search call with surname or spouseSurname: 'Halsteinsdr' (spouseSurname is the shape the live index answers -- the bride is not indexed as a principal), proving the skill tried the collection-specific surname abbreviation, not just the already-fixed given-name variant.

DO NOT grade whether a record_search call sent an abbreviated surname. The deterministic validator test_surname_variant_hints_followed reads the tool calls and decides it: a run that never set surname or spouseSurname to an abbreviated form of 'Halsteinsdatter' fails there. The case it guards is the 2026-07-21 e2e miss, where the skill varied the given name and tried a principal-only fallback and never applied the collection's surname abbreviation, returned by record_search as surnameVariantHints on the nil.

Correctness: score 3 if the reply reports the positive match and correctly attributes it to Anders Monsen (LKFW-9XH) / Unna Halsteinsdatter (KZHH-VTX). Score 2 if the skill stumbles onto the record without a deliberate surname-abbreviation attempt (e.g. by dropping every filter until only collectionId remains and eyeballing an unfiltered dump) -- this technically finds the record but doesn't demonstrate applying the collection's surname abbreviation (from references/collection-quirks.md or surnameVariantHints).

Tool Arguments: the validator above decides whether an abbreviated surname was sent. Grade the rest: expect a record_search call against collectionId '1468080' carrying subjectId 'LKFW-9XH' so the pool is ranked inline.

This test isolates the surname half of the same collection-quirks.md 'vary both together' instruction that ut_search_records_022 isolates for the given-name half. Passing 022 does not imply passing this test -- a skill that only ever varies the given name will fail here even though it now passes 022. Do not treat a call that varies ONLY the given name as satisfying this test's ground truth, however many such calls are made.
Log quality: the negative surname-unvaried attempts and the eventual surname-abbreviated attempt should each produce their own research_log_append entry, not be collapsed into one.

record_read is stocked but OPTIONAL. The marriage record's full content is already in the search response's gedcomx, so the skill may report from the search hit or may read the record first — reading it before reporting is sound practice, not a defect. Score neither path down. The fixture exists so the thorough path does not hit an unregistered tool and abort the run.
